messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: auth anomaly detected for service account svc-ingest. Multiple failed and successful token exchanges from 3 distinct foreign IP ranges. Suspicious uploaded artifact to s3://redwood-temp-debug/ that contains plaintext debug logs. Auto-priority: P1. Please acknowledge.

anne: Acked. I'm on-call. Can someone pull the artifact and confirm what's in the logs?

ivan: On it. I'm running a quick grep against the object (don't cat in-channel). Preliminary: found 3 long-looking API keys and multiple bearer tokens. Keys appear to be long-lived service keys, likely from svc-ingest.

raj: Adding: the uploads originated from an ephemeral EC2 in prod-us-east-1 tagged "data-debugger". IPs are 45.76.9.101, 93.184.216.34, and 203.0.113.77. Possible compromised dev workstation or CI runner.

maya: Support: any active customer impact? Are we seeing spikes in auth failures or user-facing errors?

ivan: We see a gap: no obvious user-facing 5xxes. But there's a spike of unauthorized attempts against the ingestion API (500 req/min over baseline). Could be credential stuffing with exposed keys. Recommend immediate key rotation for svc-ingest and revoke active tokens.

anne: Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Revoke/rotate svc-ingest keys. 2) Block the 3 IPs at edge and talk to infra for temporary ACL. 3) Revoke any sessions issued in the last 24h for svc-ingest. 4) Notify customers if any tokens belonged to customer-managed keys (TBD).

raj: Working on network blocks now. Pushing WAF rule to drop traffic from the three IPs and adding rate-limit 10r/s for /v1/ingest. Pushing in 30s.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: waf-rule/18076 -> all-edge (canary -> 2 regions). CI link: https://ci.internal/redwood/18076

ivan: Key rotation steps (internal playbook snippet):

```
# rotate AWS-styled service key for svc-ingest
aws iam update-access-key --user-name svc-ingest --access-key-id <OLD_KEY> --status Inactive
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-ingest
# store new keys in KMS-backed secret store
secretctl put --name /services/svc-ingest/creds --value "<NEW_KEY>:<NEW_SECRET>" --kms key-arn
# rotate app config and restart ingest workers
kubectl set env deploy/ingest-worker -n prod SVC_INGEST_KEY=<NEW_KEY>
kubectl rollout restart deploy/ingest-worker -n prod
```

ivan: Also revoking active bearer tokens via internal admin: POST /admin/sessions/revoke {"service":"svc-ingest", "since":"2026-03-14T00:00:00Z"}

anne: Raj/ivan, priority: make rotation atomic so we don't break producers. Can we issue a new key, push to secrets, then flip? Avoid double-fail.

raj: Yes. Plan: create new key, push to secret store with same key name but new version, wait 90s for ingestion clients to pick it up (we have 60s TTL on secrets refresh), then retire old key. Rolling restart only if clients don't pick up automatically.

maya: If this affects customers, I've drafted a short status update we can send via Statuspage and workspace messages. Statuspage draft: "Investigating suspicious auth activity affecting ingestion pipeline. We have temporarily rotated service credentials and mitigations are in place. No confirmed data exfiltration of customer stored content; we are continuing our investigation and will update within 2 hours." Want legal/security eyes before posting.

ivan: Legal looped. Sec is preparing an incident ticket and will tag compliance. Also collecting hashes of leaked object for chain of custody. Object path: s3://redwood-temp-debug/debug-2026-03-14-09.gz, md5: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184 (saved to internal evidence bucket, read-only).

anne: Can we get a list of internal services that have svc-ingest keys? Who issued these keys originally?

raj: Looks like two CI pipelines and a single long-running ingest-runner from 2025-10-01. Owner tags: @ci-team, @data-platform. I'm pinging both owners.

ivan: Triage notes: credential exposure -> medium likelihood of downstream misuse. No confirmed customer data access yet. We should assume keys are compromised and rotate. Also enable aggressive logging for subsequent 48h: increase auth audit logging level to DEBUG for ingestion endpoints.

anne: Action items assigned:
- ivan: rotate keys, revoke tokens, keep evidence artifacts (IN PROGRESS)
- raj: block IPs, push WAF, coordinate secret rollout (IN PROGRESS)
- maya: prepare customer comms and support runbook (PENDING legal)
- anne: incident commander, coordinate handoff to day shift at 0600 UTC (IN PROGRESS)

maya: Support runbook snippet (for reps):
- If asked: confirm we rotated service credentials, temporary mitigation in place, monitoring ongoing.
- Avoid saying "breach" until Sec confirms. Use: "security incident under investigation."

ivan: Quick commands to revoke tokens (internal API):

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEC_ADMIN" -d '{"service":"svc-ingest","revoke_since":"2026-03-14T00:00:00Z"}' https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/sessions/revoke

# verify tokens revoked
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEC_ADMIN" https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/sessions?service=svc-ingest | jq .active_count


raj: WAF rule deployed canary succeeded. Rolling to all-edge in 4m. Blocks seen: 45.76.9.101 had 23 blocked requests in canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: waf-rule/18076 -> all-edge (duration 00:03:12)

anne: Ivan status?

ivan: New key created and stored. Triggered secret refresh. Active token revocation call returned 204. Active_count now 0 from admin API. Starting key retirement in 5m. Logging toggled to DEBUG for /v1/ingest. Evidence saved.

maya: Support draft updated with legal language and ready for post once anne gives go.

anne: Handing off to day shift: @oncall-day (simon) please take over. Summary for handoff: rotated svc-ingest keys, revoked sessions, blocked three malicious IPs at WAF, increased auth logging, artifact saved for forensics. No confirmed customer data exfiltration; monitoring continues. Pager pinned to incident channel for follow-ups.

simon (via oncall-day): Acked. Taking lead. Will verify all mitigations and start root cause investigation with data-platform and CI teams.

ivan: Follow-ups for next 24h: 1) full scan of s3 buckets for leaked artifacts referencing svc-ingest keys, 2) rotate any other long-lived keys issued to same owner, 3) rotate CI runner tokens, 4) customer notification plan if evidence of customer data access is found.

anne: Closing notes for thread: created incident ticket IC-2026-0452, severity P1 -> security. Assigning to ivan/raj/simon for execution. Will update statuspage if we find customer impact.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: https://tracker.internal/redwood/IC-2026-0452

maya: Thanks team. I'll prepare a short FAQ for support with templated responses.

ivan: Leaving a final checklist in the ticket (evidence saved, keys rotated, logging increased, IPs blocked, owners contacted). Will attach forensic timeline later.

anne: Thanks all. If anything new, post in this thread. :lock:
